messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: P99 latency spike detected for customer Cobalt (vpc-cobalt-01) in eu-west-1. p95=1.1s p99=7.9s, queued requests rising. Alert rule: dedicated-pool-latency > 5s for 5m. dashboard: https://console.redwood.dev/d/alerts/cobalt-vpc

sam: ack — paging oncall. I’m on it. quick glance: errors are low, just high tail latency and request backlog.

alex: oncall here. is this scoped to Cobalt only or multi-tenant? any error spikes + customer-visible failures?

mira: scoped to vpc-cobalt-01 dedicated pool in eu-west-1 only. I see no 500s in the request logs, just long queue wait times and very high GPU utilization (~96%).

jon: initial hypothesis: batching backlog + KV cache misses. Cobalt's workload has long context lengths this morning (median seq len ~1200 -> larger KV load). Kernel selection cost also went up for that traffic.

sam: grabbing pool state now — running scale command: ```
# rwdctl pools describe vpc-cobalt-01 --region eu-west-1
Name: vpc-cobalt-01
Replicas: 2
Queue depth: 430
GPU util: 95.8%
Avg batch latency: 420ms
Current model: open-redwood-xl-32b-q4
```

alex: thanks. short-term mitigation options: 1) scale pool replicas, 2) activate routing to secondary region (eu-central-1) for a fraction of traffic, 3) enable fallback to quantized smaller variant for cobalt only. Need order-of-ops and risk assessment.

tia: note — cross-region routing requires Cobalt's cross-region allowlist. I have their account SID; I can ping them for immediate approval. Without approval we can't send customer data cross-region (compliance).

mira: trying scale now — running scale command: ```
# rwdctl pools scale --pool vpc-cobalt-01 --replicas 4 --region eu-west-1
Scaling replicas: 2 -> 4
Allocating GPUs...
Replica 3 ready
Replica 4 ready
```

incident-bot: update: deployment events logged. replica health OK.

sam: after scale: queue depth dropped from 430 -> 110 in ~45s. p99 dropped to ~3.5s, p95 ~1.0s. Improvement visible but still above SLO (SLO p99 = 2s for Cobalt).

jon: while scale helps, we should reduce per-request cost: enable per-tenant model fallback for Cobalt to `open-redwood-xl-16b-q4` for 20% of traffic (canary) and shadow 10% to collect quality metrics. Plan: set routing rule with gradual rollout.

alex: +1. but we must coordinate with Cobalt support for canary. tia — did they respond?

tia: pinged Cobalt at +44-77X-XXXX; they replied: "approve canary to eu-central and smaller model for up to 25% traffic for 2 hours". they asked to keep them in the loop.

mira: applying routing rule: ```
# rwdctl routing set --tenant cobalt --rule "route 20% -> open-redwood-xl-16b-q4 (eu-west-1), 10% mirror -> eu-central-1" 
Applied routing rule for tenant cobalt
```

sam: canary started. telemetry: p99 for canary cohort ~2.2s. main cohort p99 ~3.1s. overall p99 trending down.

jon: additional tweak — KV-cache hit ratio low for cobalt (hit 18%). I'm increasing prefix cache TTL from 30s -> 120s for cobalt only to reduce KV regen. This is a moderate risk (stale prefixes) but should cut token compute overhead.

mira: applied cache TTL change for tenant cobalt. metrics show cache hits slowly climbing.

incident-bot: notification: rota update — sam acknowledged at 03:02Z, alex on-call as primary.

sam: handing off live ops to alex. My shift ends in ~30m, I'm leaving runbook notes below. @alex — I’ll stay reachable for 15m for questions.

alex: taking over. summary notes: - scaled pool 2->4 (immediate improvement) - started 20% model-fallback canary and 10% mirror to eu-central - increased tenant cache TTL - customer approved cross-region canary - current p99 ~2.1s and trending down.

alex: immediate next actions: 1) monitor p99 for 15m, 2) if p99 < 2.0s for 10m, gradually roll fallback to 50% and consider leaving 25% permanently until root cause fixed, 3) schedule post-incident debug with infra team to look at kernel/runtime behavior for long contexts.

jon: also flag for ML infra: model memory pressure + KV eviction patterns. create an issue with logs and kernel traces -> tagging @ml-infra.

mira: creating post-incident ticket: https://jira.redwood.dev/browse/INC-4872 — includes heap/profiler dumps and pool metrics.

sam: customer note drafted, sending update to Cobalt SRE: "We've mitigated the immediate tail latency by scaling and routing fallbacks. We're monitoring and will follow up with a post-incident RCA and long-term fixes." Sending now.

tia: thanks team. leaving the thread but monitoring via pager.

alex: thanks all. keeping this open until SLO stable for 30m and then we'll mark resolved and attach RCA. If p99 spikes above 3s again, re-open and escalate to infra oncall.

incident-bot: THREAD STATUS: open -> monitoring. next automated check in 5m.
